articles.headline: Cowboys say sick Joey Porter Jr. won't face Bucs on 'TNF'
articles.description: Joey Porter Jr. was ruled out of Thursday night's game against the Tampa Bay Buccaneers because of an illness.
articles.body:
ARLINGTON, Texas -- Joey Porter Jr.'s home debut for the Dallas Cowboys will have to wait.

Porter was ruled out of Thursday night's game against the Tampa Bay Buccaneers because of an illness, with the team announcing the decision roughly 1 hour, 45 minutes before the 8:15 p.m. ET kickoff. Porter arrived at the stadium before getting examined and being ruled out.

Acquired from the Pittsburgh Steelers last week, Porter played 24 snaps in Sunday's win against the Houston Texans despite only practicing three days. The Cowboys had two brief workouts this week with the quick turnaround in facing the Bucs.

Without Porter, the Cowboys likely will have to start second-year cornerback Shavon Revel, who has been dealing with knee and ankle issues he suffered in a Week 3 loss to the Baltimore Ravens in Rio de Janeiro. Reddy Steward has been activated from the practice squad for the third straight game, and the Cowboys also have Ameer Speed and Caelen Carson active.

Week 1 starter Cobie Durant will miss his third consecutive game with a hamstring strain but could return in Week 6 against the Green Bay Packers.

In order for the Cowboys to give up their 2027 sixth-round pick as part of the Steelers trade, Porter needs to be active for two games. That at least extends to next week due to his illness.

articles.headline: Unbeaten, defense-led Vikings head south to face the struggling Saints and QB Tyler Shough
articles.description: — Saints quarterback Tyler Shough's 14th career start will be among the toughest tests of his young career — and he knows it.
articles.body:
NEW ORLEANS -- — Saints quarterback Tyler Shough's 14th career start will be among the toughest tests of his young career — and he knows it.


              “There is going to be times where Minnesota is going to get us,” Shough said this week after studying the Vikings' blitz-heavy defense, which ranks first in the NFL in sacks with 16. 


              “They are going to make good plays,” Shough continued, “but we cannot let that compound into another play.”


              New Orleans (1-3) is desperate to close out a three-game homestand with a victory after dropping its previous two games, the latest in lopsided fashion to rival Atlanta last Monday night.


              A victory over the Vikings (4-0) on Sunday in the Superdome could go a long way toward restoring confidence in the direction the Saints are headed under second-year coach Kellen Moore. 


              All the Saints have to do is figure out how to score on a Minnesota defense that has allowed an NFL-low 12.8 points per game.


              “It's going to be a really good challenge,” Shough said. “We get a really good chance to kind of show what we can do.”


              Vikings defensive coordinator Brian Flores said the key to his unit's success has been his personnel. 


              “It’s their defense, not mine,” Flores said. “We’ve got a lot of guys who get it, and we’re all working together.”


              Linebacker Blake Cashman gives Flores credit for being innovative and increasing the roles of players who show they can handle that.


              The result is not only frequent blitzing, but pass-rush schemes that are disguised and can feature a variety of players.


              “It's obviously a great scheme and they also have great players that understand what is being asked of them,” Saints guard David Edwards said. “The stress comes with identifying who’s coming.”


              Meanwhile, Edwards, who spent the previous three seasons with the contending Buffalo Bills and was part of two Super Bowl teams with the Los Angeles Rams before that, said he has been gratified by the Saints' response to their poor showing against the Falcons.


              “The message hasn’t changed. The process hasn’t changed — and that’s the hallmark of a winning operation,” Edwards said. “Games like that may happen, but it’s your response and your approach to the next week that matters.”


              Similarly, Vikings linebacker Eric Wilson said his team is trying to guard against complacency after coming out of the gate fast.


              “You can’t get too high on your high horse or else you get humbled really quick,” Wilson said. “We have to be really critical of ourselves, especially in times like these.”


              Need to know
              Minnesota (4-0) at New Orleans (1-3).


              When/where to watch: Sunday, 1 p.m. EDT, Fox.


              Latest odds: Vikings by 1 1/2.


              Against the spread: Vikings 3-

articles.headline: NFL Week 5 arrivals: Cowboys show Dallas Stars love ahead of TNF
articles.description: NFL stars continue to turn game-day arrivals into their own weekly fashion showcase.
articles.body:
Week 5 of the NFL season is here, and October is starting to bring a little more variety to the forecast -- and potentially to pregame fashion.

With fall temperatures settling into parts of the country and lingering heat beginning to ease elsewhere, players have another opportunity to switch up their game-day looks. 

California's early-October heat wave is expected to weaken, while cooler conditions in the Northeast and a hurricane that could bring heavy rain to parts of the South make for a mixed bag across the country this weekend. That leaves room for everything from lightweight fits to layered looks as players make their stadium entrances.

Whether they're embracing the season with jackets and sweaters or sticking to their signature styles, NFL players are bringing another round of personality to the tunnel in Week 5.

Thursday night drip

Dallas Cowboys teammates Cooper Beebe and Brevyn Spann-Ford showed some love to the Dallas Stars ahead of "Thursday Night Football." Beebe arrived in a Jake Oettinger jersey, while Spann-Ford repped Stars legend Mike Modano.

articles.headline: Bears have opportunity to show again they've gained the upper hand in their rivalry with Packers
articles.description: — After beating the Green Bay Packers for the NFC North title and knocking them out of the playoffs last season, the Chicago Bears have one more opportunity to show definitively that a new chapter has started in the NFL’s most-played rivalry.
articles.body:
GREEN BAY, Wis. -- — After beating the Green Bay Packers for the NFC North title and knocking them out of the playoffs last season, the Chicago Bears have one more opportunity to show definitively that a new chapter has started in the NFL’s most-played rivalry.


              Chicago has won three of its past four meetings with the Packers, who had beaten the Bears 11 straight times from 2019-24. The Bears beat the Packers 22-16 in overtime last December after scoring 10 points in the final two minutes of regulation and then erased a 21-3 halftime deficit to beat them again 31-27 in the NFC wild-card playoffs.


              The quarterback who led both those comebacks won't be playing Sunday when the Bears (3-1) meet the Packers (2-2) again at Lambeau Field. Tyson Bagent is expected to start in place of Caleb Williams, who has missed Chicago’s past two games with a hamstring injury.


              “To say this is just like any game just wouldn’t be true,” Bagent said. “This is one of the greatest rivalries in all of sports.”


              Ben Johnson’s arrival as the Bears coach last season has spiced up this series.


              Johnson’s locker room speech following the Bears’ playoff win over Green Bay gained lots of traction on social media as video showed him shouting an expletive before adding “the Packers.”


              Packers linebacker Zaire Franklin is new to this rivalry, yet he already understands the harsh feelings between these teams.


              “It’s a lot of bad blood — a lot of bad blood,” said Franklin, who came to Green Bay this year after spending eight seasons in Indianapolis. “A lot of genuine dislike, which is a little different than nowadays. Nowadays, most rivalries are just on social media, and in the offseason, you’re hanging out. I don’t think nobody wants to hang out with the Bears in the offseason.”


              While Chicago has overcome Williams’ injury to start fast, the Packers are having a tougher time dealing with the absences of key players.


              Green Bay has lost linebacker Edgerrin Cooper (Achilles tendon), offensive tackle Zach Bako-Bewele (knee) and wide receiver Jayden Reed (neck) to season-ending injuries.


              All-Pro edge rusher Micah Parsons hasn't played yet this season as he recovers from a torn anterior cruciate ligament. Green Bay’s running game has struggled without Josh Jacobs, who is on the commissioner’s exempt list after pleading no contest to two misdemeanor charges stemming from a May altercation with his then-girlfriend.


              Green Bay could get over .500 for the first time this season by avenging those two losses to the Bears and perhaps silencing Johnson for the time being.


              “I mean, he’s dissing us,” Packers offensive tackle Jordan Morgan said. “He’s dissing the Packers. A lot of people in here, I’m pretty sure, take that to heart. And we’ve got a chance to prove to everybody on Sunday that we’re the best

articles.headline: Broncos seek first AFC West win as Chargers try to avoid an 0-5 start
articles.description: — Something's got to give when the Denver Broncos and Los Angeles Chargers...
articles.body:
INGLEWOOD, Calif. -- — Something's got to give when the Denver Broncos and Los Angeles Chargers meet on Sunday. Either the Broncos will earn their first AFC West win or the Chargers will extricate themselves from a crowded NFL basement.


              Led by quarterback Bo Nix, the Broncos (2-2) have slumped offensively, ranking both 27th in scoring and in total yards per game.


              “Certainly this isn't championship football,” said Denver coach Sean Payton, who decided this week to take back offensive play-calling duties.


              Chargers coach Jim Harbaugh could say the same about his team, which has been plagued by penalties and turnovers.


              One of the league's five winless teams, the Chargers are looking to avoid an 0-5 start for the first time since 2003. Meanwhile, the Broncos are seeking their first win at SoFi Stadium since 2023.


              Both teams' offensive coordinators are on the spot. Davis Webb's stint calling plays for the Broncos lasted just four games.


              Mike McDaniel's tenure has gotten off to a rocky start, with the Los Angeles offense averaging 16.8 points, which is 29th in the league. The Chargers have used a three-man rotation at running back for the last two games.


              “It's an advantage to the Chargers with defenses having to prepare three different tackling plans for backs with various skill sets,” McDaniel said. “If you don't disperse the carries, it's very rare in this day and age that guys are available every week.”


              Chargers wide receiver Ladd McConkey is dealing with a the same foot injury that limited him in practice last week and also in Sunday’s game at Seattle.


              McDaniel and Payton meet again
              McDaniel was Miami's coach when the Dolphins routed Payton's Broncos 70-20 in Week 3 of the 2023 season. It was the most points scored by an NFL team in a game since 1966. The Dolphins racked up 726 yards of offense (350 rushing, 376 passing). McDaniel chose to take a knee rather than kick a late field goal that could have broken the single-game scoring record.


              Payton joked that he was a having a good day until it was brought up this week.


              “It’s a different offense a little bit,” he said. “That’s one of those games where we turned it over offensively, but you get burned a few times and you don’t touch the stove again.”


              Need to know
              Denver (2-2) at Los Angeles Chargers (0-4).

              Latest odds: Broncos by 3 1/2.

              Series record: Broncos lead 73-58-1.

articles.headline: Kirk Cousins and Raiders look to build on fast start against Patriots defense dealing with injuries
articles.description: — Kirk Cousins' torrid start to the season has been one of the NFL's biggest surprises.
articles.body:
FOXBOROUGH, Mass. -- — Kirk Cousins' torrid start to the season has been one of the NFL's biggest surprises. 


              The 38-year-old Las Vegas Raiders quarterback is looking to keep it going this week at New England against a Patriots defense that is suddenly having trouble keeping its secondary healthy.


              Despite his first loss of the season last week against Kansas City, Cousins is up to 11 touchdown passes — the fastest he has reached that total through four games in his 15-year career. His previous best was 10 TDs through four games in 2018. It has helped quiet the chatter about him being simply a bridge quarterback to Fernando Mendoza, who Las Vegas took No. 1 overall in April. 


              Cousins said he's just enjoying seeing the resilience of the entire team in Klint Kubiak's first season, a group Cousins said is confirming what he observed from them going back to spring workouts.


              “These guys, they want to do it the right way. Football means something to them,” Cousins said. "They’re hardworking, listen well, and it makes it a joy to be the quarterback for a group of guys like that. But yo'veu got to go prove it again every week.”


              That next challenge is a Patriots team whose win at Buffalo last week helped the defending AFC champions avoid a 1/3 start. That victory not only saw quarterback Drake Maye break out of an early season funk with three touchdowns, but a defense playing without star cornerback Christian Gonzalez (shoulder) was able to slow quarterback Josh Allen enough to best their division rival.


              Gonzalez sat out this week's first two practices, putting his availability in question for the second straight game. Fellow starting cornerback Carlton Davis (neck) also missed the first two practices, along with rookie Karon Prunty (hamstring). Other cornerbacks that were limited in practice to begin the week were Charles Woods (shoulder) and rookie Channing Canada (hamstring).


              Whoever is available Sunday, Maye said carrying as much of the momentum they can from last week is the goal.


              “You would like to say everybody — especially on offense — you’d like to say that the first three weeks weren’t what we wanted to put out there,” Maye said. "You have to try to build off last week, knowing that it’s not just going to do it for you. You have to put the work in and the focus, and hopefully continue to catch a trend and catch a stride.


              Need to know
              Las Vegas (3-1) at New England (2-2)


              When/where to watch: Sunday, 1 p.m. EDT, CBS.


              Latest odds: Patriots by 3 1/2.


              Against the spread: Raiders 4-0; Patriots 2-1-1.


              Last week: Raiders lost to Chiefs 30-27; Patriots beat Bills 29-26.


              Last meeting: Raiders beat Patriots 20-13 on Sept. 5, 2025, in Foxborough, Mass.


              Series record: Patriots lead 20-18-1.

articles.headline: Thunder's Gilegous-Alexander buys stake in Atlético Madrid
articles.description: Two-time NBA MVP Shai Gilgeous-Alexander has become a shareholder in Atlético Madrid, the Spanish club announced on Thursday.
articles.body:
Two-time NBA MVP Shai Gilgeous-Alexander has become a shareholder in Atlético Madrid, the Spanish club announced on Thursday.

In a statement, Atlético, who are currently second in LaLiga, said their partnership with the Oklahoma City Thunder guard, 28, was "grounded in shared values: ambition, excellence and the belief that every result must be earned."

Atlético have been majority owned by the US-based fund Apollo Global Management since last year.

"I'm excited to officially join Atlético Madrid's ownership group," Gilgeous-Alexander said. "This is a club with a long-standing presence at the top of European football, and I'm grateful for the opportunity to be part of its future."

The club did not disclose the size of Gilgeous-Alexander's ownership stake.

The Canadian, who was pictured wearing an Atlético tracksuit earlier this year, was traded to the Thunder in 2019, after spending a season with the LA Clippers.

He won the 2025 NBA finals, being named MVP, and won his second MVP title a year later as the Thunder were eliminated in the Western Conference Finals.

Gilgeous-Alexander also played for Canada at the 2024 Olympics.

Atlético are one of Spain's most successful football clubs, most recently winning LaLiga in 2014 and 2021 under current coach Diego Simeone.

Gilgeous-Alexander joins a number of high-profile NBA players who have invested in football, including LeBron James and Kevin Durant.

articles.headline: Tyrese Maxey, Jaylen Brown, VJ Edgecombe make 'Abbott Elementary' cameos
articles.description: "Abbott Elementary" continues to embrace Philadelphia sports culture with its latest instance starring the 76ers.
articles.body:
Tyrese Maxey, VJ Edgecombe and Jaylen Brown made a surprise appearance on the season premiere of "Abbott Elementary" on Wednesday night, but their visit to the fictional Philadelphia school didn't exactly go as planned.

The cameo occurred during a scene in which history teacher Jacob Hill (played by Chris Perfetti) made an Instagram post asking the Philadelphia 76ers to build a playground at Abbott Elementary. Hill had learned that the Philadelphia Eagles build a free playground for a local school each year, but the team had already selected another school.

After a group of impostors wearing Sixers jerseys convinced Hill they were bench players for the team, the real NBA stars arrived to answer his request. 

Maxey introduced himself, Edgecombe and the team's "new guy," Brown, telling Hill that he'd seen his Instagram post and found it "very effective."

There was just one problem: Hill, who isn't particularly familiar with men's sports, didn't recognize them.

"If you're the Sixers, then where's LeBron James?" Hill asked.

"This is going to sound like a lie, but he's actually running up the 'Rocky' steps right now," Maxey replied.

"He loves that movie," Brown added.

Unconvinced, Hill dismissed the trio.

"Yeah, right. Get the hell out of here, you tall jerks," he said.

As the players walked away, Hill made the admission:

"I really got to start watching men's sports."

Ahead of the Season 6 premiere, "Abbott Elementary" creator and star Quinta Brunson, a West Philadelphia native who plays second-grade teacher Janine Teagues, shared a photo with the three players on Instagram. Maxey responded in the comments with a goat emoji.

The NBA trio joins a growing list of Philadelphia sports figures who have appeared on the ABC comedy.

Philadelphia Eagles quarterback Jalen Hurts made a virtual appearance during the Season 3 premiere in February 2024, alongside former teammates Jason Kelce and Brandon Graham. Eagles wide receiver DeVonta Smith has also appeared on the show.

Philadelphia Phillies slugger Kyle Schwarber appeared in an episode filmed at Citizens Bank Park last season, while Philadelphia Flyers mascot Gritty was in the Season 2 premiere.

The Sixers have also been part of the show's storylines before. Brunson's character once dressed as former Philadelphia guard James Harden for Halloween, and the teachers competed for courtside Sixers tickets in a Season 2 episode. Former Sixers player Andre Iguodala also made an appearance as a fictional love interest of principal Ava Coleman (played by Janelle James).

articles.headline: Man City manager Enzo Maresca says he 'trusts the club completely'
articles.description: Enzo Maresca has said he "trusts the club completely" in his first interview since Manchester City were found guilty of breaking financial rules.
articles.body:
Enzo Maresca has said he "trusts the club completely" in his first interview since Manchester City were found guilty of breaking financial rules.

Maresca is preparing his players for the trip to Liverpool on Sunday -- City's first game since the publication of the damning judgement in their case with the Premier League.

The Italian spoke to in-house media on Thursday. He's due to hold his first news conference with reporters since the verdict on Friday morning.

"Personally, I'm very calm to be honest," said Maresca.

"The club has been quite clear. We trust completely the club.

"We understand the noise, but the focus for us is just what we can control and we can control just the football side."

Despite the guilty verdict, both chairman Khaldoon Al-Mubarak and CEO Ferran Soriano have insisted the club are innocent. A formal appeal has been launched.

The bulk of City's players have been away on international duty during the break. Now back at the CFA, Maresca insists they are "focused" despite intense spotlight on the Etihad Stadium.

"The feeling is fantastic, to be honest," Maresca said.

"The players are excited for the next two games. But especially they are excited because in this moment we are top of the league.

"The players are just focused on that. They know what we can control is the football side -- they are not worried at all about different things.

"They know their profession and they know that the noise is there, but they don't care too much about the noise. They are just focused in this moment on how we can beat Liverpool and how, together with the fans, we can try to win in Anfield."

articles.headline: Sources: 76ers plan to play starters in preseason game vs. Nets
articles.description: The 76ers plan to play their starters Thursday against the Nets, sources told ESPN.
articles.body:
NEW YORK -- The Philadelphia 76ers plan to play their starters Thursday against the Brooklyn Nets, sources told ESPN, giving fans a first preseason glimpse of LeBron James in a Sixers uniform.

Sixers coach Nick Nurse told reporters that if all of his main players came through Wednesday's practice healthy, he hoped to play "the majority" of them -- namely James, Joel Embiid, Tyrese Maxey, Jaylen Brown and VJ Edgecombe -- together in the first half against the Nets.

James, Embiid and Maxey were healthy scratches in Philadelphia's preseason-opening victory Monday against the New York Knicks.

Brown scored 22 points in 17 minutes Monday while Edgecombe had 12 points and seven assists in 20 minutes.

articles.headline: Fantasy basketball: Category league draft tiers
articles.description: Eric Moody groups players into tiers by each position for category-based leagues.
articles.body:
Category leagues require a different approach than points leagues. Volume still matters, but it isn't everything. Steals and blocks are harder to find, while 3-pointers can be concentrated among certain types of players. Field goal percentage, free throw percentage and turnovers can quietly swing a league over the course of a season.

That can change how players should be valued.

A guard who gives you steals, 3-pointers and strong percentages can be more valuable than a higher-scoring player who hurts you elsewhere. A center who blocks shots without wrecking your free throw percentage can give you a major advantage. A forward who provides assists can help solve a shortage in a category that is harder to address at that position.

Our recent 10-team roto mock showed how that can play out. Four point guards went in the first round, while no small forwards were selected. Then Cooper Flagg, Scottie Barnes and Amen Thompson went with three of the first four picks of Round 2. Point guard became a focus again in Round 3, when James Harden, Jalen Brunson, Josh Giddey, LaMelo Ball, Jamal Murray and Stephen Curry all came off the board in a seven-pick span.

Derrick White also went 17th overall, which makes sense given how difficult his combination of 3s, assists, steals and blocks is to replace at shooting guard. Power forward showed one of the clearest positional drop-offs, while center remained deep enough that useful rebounders and shot-blockers were still available well into the middle rounds.

That's where tiers become useful.

I've separated players by their default position, even if they qualify at multiple spots. The rankings show how I value the players in a neutral build. The tiers show where the player pool changes. Once the draft starts, what you already have should influence what comes next.

The goal isn't simply to draft the highest-ranked player every round. It's to know from round to round what your team does well, where it is vulnerable and when a category or position is about to become much harder to draft.

The rankings tell you who I like. The tiers tell you when you need to act. Your roster tells you who fits best.

articles.headline: Fantasy basketball: Points league draft tiers
articles.description: Eric Moody groups players into tiers by each position for points leagues.
articles.body:
In our recent 10-team points mock draft, the first round leaned heavily toward point guards and big men. Four point guards came off the board, along with three power forwards and two centers. Anthony Edwards was the only shooting guard selected, and no small forwards were taken. The first small forward didn't go until Amen Thompson at No. 13 overall, followed by Scottie Barnes and Cooper Flagg later in the second round.

By the middle of the draft, the board looked much different. Round 6 alone featured four small forwards: Caleb Wilson, Brandon Miller, Franz Wagner and Trey Murphy III. That tells you a lot about this year's player pool. Point guards and big men are prominent near the top, while much of the wing depth shows up later. That doesn't mean you have to force a small forward early, but you should know where each position starts to thin out.

Point guard gives you more room to wait. My third tier alone includes Tyrese Maxey, Jalen Brunson, Trae Young, Josh Giddey, Devin Booker, Tyrese Haliburton, James Harden, LaMelo Ball and Jamal Murray. If several of those players are still available, there may be no reason to reach for the position.

Small forward is different. The position has useful depth later, but the top options disappear quickly. Power forward also has a large middle group, while center is more concentrated near the top, with Nikola Jokic in his own tier and Victor Wembanyama right behind him.

This is where the board starts to matter more than the rankings. A straight ranking tells you who I value more. Tiers tell you where the drop-offs are. If several point guards remain in the same tier but only one small forward is left before a drop, that should factor into your pick. The same applies when a position has enough depth to let you wait another round.

The tiers below are based on our preseason projections and show where we see the biggest breaks at each position. The idea is simple: know where you can wait and where waiting too long could cost you.

Point guard

Thoughts on PGs:

Gilgeous-Alexander is projected for 31.3 PPG, 6.4 APG and 1.7 SPG, while Doncic is projected for 33.0 PPG, 8.9 APG and 8.5 RPG. Gilgeous-Alexander has the stronger durability track record, while Doncic brings elite production across points, rebounds and assists.

Cunningham stands alone in Tier 2. He finished sixth in fantasy points per game last season and is projected for 24.6 PPG and 9.8 APG.

The depth starts in Tier 3 with Maxey, Brunson, Young, Giddey, Booker and Haliburton. Haliburton could outperform this group if he returns to form after missing last season.

Harden, Ball and Murray make up Tier 4 and give managers another strong group if they wait at the position. Ball brings plenty of upside in Minnesota, while Harden and Murray remain reliable fantasy options.

There are also a few younger guards worth watching later, including Harper and Acuff Jr.

articles.headline: Mikel Arteta: 'I still have the scar' from Arsenal's Champions League final defeat
articles.description: Mikel Arteta has said he still has a "scar" from Arsenal's Champions League final defeat to Paris Saint-Germain in May.
articles.headlineJa: ミケル・アルテタ「アーセナルのCL決勝敗戦の傷跡は今も残っている」
articles.descriptionJa: ミケル・アルテタは、5月に行われたパリ・サンジェルマンとのチャンピオンズリーグ決勝での敗戦による「傷跡」がいまだに残っていると語った。
articles.body:
Mikel Arteta has said he still has a "scar" from Arsenal's Champions League final defeat to Paris Saint-Germain in May.

The Spaniard, whose new four-year contract at the Emirates was announced on Wednesday, took the club to their first Champions League final for 20 years last season but saw his team defeated on penalties after a 1-1 draw.

Echoing the words of the last man to take them to the brink of elite European glory -- Arsène Wenger, who previously said that "every defeat is a scar in your heart" -- Arteta told The Athletic: "I still have the scar, like Arsène says.

"I still have that poison in my veins. It has to stay there because that's when you learn and that probably is going to be a massive driver for me and everybody."

Looking towards the future, Arteta added that he was excited for a number of different aspects of the club's growth.

"Globally, with our supporters? Great. How are we going to build the next three squads? Great. How the rules of the game are going to change us, and how we're going to stay ahead of that to take advantage? Great," he said.

"But this is going to happen if every single day we look after what we built. We make it a little bit better, like software that is upgrading and upgrading. When can it stop is infinite."

He added: "It feels like it's still a lot to do, and it's just the beginning."

Arteta has, however, already managed to do something no Arsenal manager had achieved for 22 years: win a league title.

"It wasn't just a trophy. It was a moment that we're going to remember for the rest of our lives," he said.

Asked what game from his Arsenal tenure he would relive, the 44-year-old chose the controversial 1-0 win over West Ham which put the Gunners on the brink of returning to the top of the perch.

"This is football elevated to its best version, when a journey, a moment that can change so many people's lives, goes one way or the other," he said. "You just pray because you know if it goes the wrong side, probably it's gone again.

"That day when I went home, I said, 'We're going to be champions. It is our year. This has happened for a reason, and we're going to get it done.'"

Arsenal return from the international break in Saturday's early kickoff against Leeds United at the Emirates, looking to return to the top of the table ahead of Manchester City's trip to Liverpool on Sunday.
